claims.text: Post-fabrication deep cryogenic treatment of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components will improve both dimensional precision and mechanical integrity.
The improvements arise from residual-stress relief and beneficial phase transitions that reduce internal defects.
HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy can be produced by laser melting deposition.
As-built additively manufactured HEA components exhibit residual stresses, porosity, uneven grain structures, and measurable dimensional deviations.
The proposed DCT consists of extended immersion in liquid nitrogen at approximately -196 °C.
DCT should be performed immediately after fabrication under ambient atmospheric conditions.
The studied additively manufactured HfNbTaTiZr alloy has a primarily BCC structure.
DCT will induce HCP precipitates at grain boundaries.
DCT will relieve lattice distortion and refine the grain structure.
DCT will decrease micro-voids or pore defects.
Rapid cooling to cryogenic temperature relieves residual stresses accumulated during laser additive manufacturing.
Cryogenic cooling triggers phase transformations and precipitate formation that refine the microstructure and improve grain-boundary metallurgical bonding.
Reducing fabrication-induced defects through DCT improves dimensional accuracy and mechanical properties.
Relative to untreated as-built parts, DCT-treated HEA parts will have smaller dimensional deviations, lower residual stresses, and fewer microstructural defects.
DCT may increase tensile strength by as much as 25% relative to the untreated additively manufactured baseline.
DCT will improve ductility relative to untreated as-deposited HEA.
Untreated additively manufactured HEA components generally have significant residual stress, dimensional inaccuracies, and a high frequency of microstructural defects.
DCT should be most effective for laser-additively-manufactured HEAs with BCC or BCC/HCP phase structures.
DCT efficacy will vary with alloy composition, processing history, treatment duration, and initial defect level.
In laser-deposited HfNbTaTiZr-based HEA, DCT induced a phase transition and increased tensile strength and elongation relative to the as-deposited alloy.
